name: STARD 2015 (diagnostic accuracy studies)
citation: Bossuyt PM et al. STARD 2015: an updated list of essential items for reporting diagnostic accuracy studies. BMJ 2015;351:h5527

items.topic: Identification as a diagnostic accuracy study

items.question: Is the abstract a structured summary of design, methods, results and conclusions (see STARD for Abstracts)?

items.topic: Background and intended use of the index test
items.question: Are the scientific and clinical background given, with the intended use and clinical role of the index test?
Are the study objectives and hypotheses stated?
Does the text say whether data collection was planned before or after the tests were performed?
Are the participants' eligibility criteria stated?
Is it stated on what basis potentially eligible participants were identified?
Are the setting, location and dates of identification given?
Is the series type stated for the participants as enrolled, not only mentioned?

items.topic: Index test and reference standard in detail
items.question: Are the index test and the reference standard described in enough detail to replicate them?
Is the choice of reference standard justified where alternatives exist?
Are cut-offs or categories defined for both tests, separating pre-specified from exploratory ones?
Does the text say what clinical information and other test results each reader or assessor had?
Are the methods for estimating or comparing accuracy measures described?
Is the handling of indeterminate index test or reference standard results described?
Is the handling of missing index test or reference standard data described?
Are analyses of variability in accuracy described, separating pre-specified from exploratory ones?
Is the intended sample size given with how it was determined?
Is the flow of participants reported, using a diagram?
Are the participants' baseline demographic and clinical characteristics reported?
Are disease severity (with the condition) and alternative diagnoses (without it) reported?
Are the time interval and any clinical interventions between index test and reference standard reported?
Are index test results cross-tabulated (or their distribution given) against the reference standard?
Is every accuracy estimate reported with its precision?
Are any adverse events from performing either test reported (or their absence stated)?
Are limitations discussed, including sources of bias, statistical uncertainty and generalisability?
Are implications for practice discussed, with the intended use and clinical role of the index test?
Are the registration number and the registry named?
Is it stated where the full study protocol can be accessed?
Are the sources of funding and other support, and the funders' role, stated?
